verdicts.reason: A has real collisions: the RSVP button and the three pills sit on top of the phone illustration. The large circle on the left is an empty dead zone, the headline block is pushed to the middle, and the legal line is jammed under the date at an illegible size. B uses a sensible three-column banner (brand and headline, then details and CTA, then the phone) with no collisions and a clear hierarchy. Its flaws: the subhead and headline crowd the bottom edge, the date, time and pill left edges don't line up, the fine print is microscopic, and the placeholder box floats next to the phone.
